cells.tense: You are carrying what you carry, and the quiet inside you is working while you do.
cells.act: walk toward what connects, leaving what does not
cells.ask: Say to someone who matters what you value in them, spoken plainly. Across the same week, drop a commitment you keep from momentum rather than meaning and leave that hour open.
cells.core:
You can bear weight and still set it down on purpose — that is the difference between lasting and stiffening. What's going better than you might notice is that your mind is getting its quiet back. Rest here isn't blankness; it's the pause that keeps you standing. That's why the load isn't costing what it could, and why you can name a day you stayed steady and a day you merely got through.

What this stretch is free to feed next is the part of staying steady that travels outward. Say what you value in someone who matters — spoken, not argued. Then go through one week watching for an obligation you keep from momentum and not meaning, and set that one down. The first puts something real between you and another person. The second shows you a weight you didn't need to take.
cells.sheetLine: Steady and still is a working pair, not a contradiction.
cells.verb: Lying still on purpose so the mind can settle
cells.place: Where you bear what must be borne, under weight, without breaking

cells.tense: You are bracing for a weight that hasn't arrived, rehearsing a burden nobody has placed on you.
cells.act: keep the heading when it is contested
cells.ask: Name a direction you have already decided and hold it through the next thing that argues. No defence, no fresh evidence. Keep walking the same way.
cells.core:
Your bearing has gone further than the load. In the hour before anything lands, you're already under it — drafting the hard conversation, hauling a weight no one handed you. The mind that was meant to rest is on night shift, checking a message twice for trouble it isn't carrying yet. In a moment you'd recognise, you've lived the difficult week before it started.

So the strength goes into rehearsals instead of into what's here. The fix isn't less thinking; it's a heading that doesn't relitigate itself. Pick a direction you've already chosen, and when the next push comes, don't reopen the decision. Moving from what you actually feel beats moving from what you fear is coming. Keep to the line you picked, and meet the load when it actually shows up.

cells.tense: You stood at a door that has already closed, still holding the frame.
cells.act: follow the pull of what might be felt, a little way
cells.ask: Go once toward something that mildly draws you — a place, a person, an hour of something. Stay a little while and decide nothing about whether it matters.
cells.core:
You can still bear weight; the trouble is what you've been bearing. Something finished is still being carried, and some part of you hasn't been told. So the days pass with a steadiness that has nothing left to steady, and the quiet that should restore you instead keeps watch at a door you already walked through.

Pushing effort or feeling into the tired place won't work — it has to come in sideways, through something that pulls. Follow one small draw a little way and see it up close. That's enough to get something moving again through the part of you that bears things, so you stand on something live instead of a shut frame. Small, once, and no verdict afterward.

cells.tense: You are keeping something steady without seeing that you are the one keeping it.
cells.act: leave the hollow ritual for the living one
cells.ask: Find a routine you keep with someone mainly because it's what you've done. If it feels hollow while you're in it, skip it once and do something alive instead — keep it small.
cells.core:
There's a steadying in your life that other people lean on, and you'd describe it as just how things are — the arrangement that happens to work, the tone that happens to hold. But keeping a thing steady is an act, and somebody is doing it. That somebody is you, and asked, you wouldn't say so.

Seeing your own part in it doesn't make the steadying heavier; it puts you beside the act instead of underneath it. Look once at a routine you keep for someone — a call, a way of showing up — and check whether it still carries anything alive between you, or only its shape. If it's only the shape, you're allowed to leave the routine and keep the person. If it's alive, you're allowed to say so.

attempts.check: The record gives no evidence about what the person's shared meanings, communities, or relationships actually are; every cell therefore speaks only about the capacity to hold and bear, and about what resting or gathering looks like in a moment they could recognise. A reader could reasonably object that 'leave the hollow ritual' assumes something is hollow — so the ask names the test as theirs (if it feels hollow), never the verdict. Both Passage asks survive being wrong: isolating the one thread that matters and leaving a form that has run out are useful even if the read about the person's state is off. The sentence that serves me more than them was a first draft's 'you are the steady one everyone leans on' — cut, because it flatters the reader's role and puts a story in their mouth. Also cut: any framing of rest as earned or owed.
